query_snapshot: What does NBS Circular 592 report about the corrosion behavior of stainless steels in sulfuric acid at approximately 150 degrees Fahrenheit across acid concentrations, and how should that affect a screening conclusion?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- NBS Circular 592 reports that molybdenum-bearing stainless steels (types 316 and 317) were the most resistant at low temperatures. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485]
- NBS Circular 592 reports that at about 150°F all of the stainless steels corrode in practically all concentrations of acid up to 95%. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485]
- NBS Circular 592 reports Roach and Hall stated that molybdenum-bearing stainless steels (316/317) were useful, at room temperature, in sulfuric acid concentrations below about 15% and above about 85%. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485]
- Therefore, stainless steels should not be treated generically as acceptable for sulfuric acid service at ≈150°F; screening should mark stainless steels as potentially unsuitable and require alloy-specific compatibility data or corrosion testing before approval. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485]
